worked_solution:
First, we expand the parenthesis and use the Pythagorean identity.

$$
\begin{aligned}{(\operatorname{sin}⁡(\frac{\pi }{12})-\operatorname{cos}⁡(\frac{\pi }{12}))}^{2} & ={sin}^{2}⁡(\frac{\pi }{12})-2\operatorname{sin}⁡(\frac{\pi }{12})\operatorname{cos}⁡(\frac{\pi }{12})+{cos}^{2}⁡(\frac{\pi }{12}) \\  & =[{sin}^{2}⁡(\frac{\pi }{12})+{cos}^{2}⁡(\frac{\pi }{12})]-2\operatorname{sin}⁡(\frac{\pi }{12})\operatorname{cos}⁡(\frac{\pi }{12}) \\  & =1-2\operatorname{sin}⁡(\frac{\pi }{12})\operatorname{cos}⁡(\frac{\pi }{12})\end{aligned}
$$

Now, let's recall the double-angle formula for sine: 

$$
2\operatorname{sin}⁡x\operatorname{cos}⁡x=\operatorname{sin}⁡2x
$$

Substituting $x=\frac{\pi }{12}$ into the above, we get

$$
\begin{aligned}2\operatorname{sin}⁡(\frac{\pi }{12})\operatorname{cos}⁡(\frac{\pi }{12}) & =\operatorname{sin}⁡(2\cdot \frac{\pi }{12}) \\  & =\operatorname{sin}⁡(\frac{\pi }{6}) \\  & =\frac{1}{2}.\end{aligned}
$$

Hence, we obtain

$$
\begin{aligned}1-2\operatorname{sin}⁡(\frac{\pi }{12})\operatorname{cos}⁡(\frac{\pi }{12}) & =1-(\frac{1}{2})=\frac{1}{2}.\end{aligned}
$$

Therefore, we conclude that

$$
{(\operatorname{sin}⁡(\frac{\pi }{12})-\operatorname{cos}⁡(\frac{\pi }{12}))}^{2}=\frac{1}{2}.
$$

EXPLANATION

First, we expand the parenthesis and use the Pythagorean identity.

(sin⁡(π12)−cos⁡(π12))2=sin2⁡(π12)−2sin⁡(π12)cos⁡(π12)+cos2⁡(π12)=[sin2⁡(π12)+cos2⁡(π12)]−2sin⁡(π12)cos⁡(π12)=1−2sin⁡(π12)cos⁡(π12)

Now, let's recall the double-angle formula for sine: 2sin⁡xcos⁡x=sin⁡2x

Substituting x=π12 into the above, we get

2sin⁡(π12)cos⁡(π12)=sin⁡(2⋅π12)=sin⁡(π6)=12.

Hence, we obtain 1−2sin⁡(π12)cos⁡(π12)=1−(12)=12.

Therefore, we conclude that (sin⁡(π12)−cos⁡(π12))2=12.
